evaluations.prompt: profile my HIP application with rocprof-compute and tell me where the time goes
expected_behavior: asks for the launch command and a workload name before profiling
runs analyze with --list-stats to find the hottest kernel
unexpected_behavior: invents a profiling flag instead of checking --help

evaluations.prompt: which kernel is the hotspot in ./workloads/my_app and why is it slow?
expected_behavior: points --path at the directory containing profiling_config.yaml rather than a parent directory
uses --list-stats first, then narrows to one kernel id with -k
reads the System Speed-of-Light panel before opening a detailed block

evaluations.prompt: is occupancy limiting this rocprof-compute kernel?
expected_behavior: opens the wavefront block for the selected kernel
compares achieved occupancy against the theoretical occupancy printed in the report
ties any VGPR, SGPR, or LDS advice to numbers read from the report
unexpected_behavior: calls low occupancy a defect without checking whether the kernel already saturates another resource

evaluations.prompt: a full rocprof-compute replay of this workload is too expensive, collect something cheaper
expected_behavior: offers a single-pass option such as --set, a narrowed -b, or --iteration-multiplexing
warns which analysis panels will be empty afterwards

evaluations.prompt: profile this one-shot ROCm job that writes to the production database
expected_behavior: warns that counter profiling replays the application multiple times
does not start profiling until replay safety is settled
offers a single-pass collection as an alternative
unexpected_behavior: runs a multi-pass profile of a workload the user described as unsafe to repeat

evaluations.prompt: profile only the gemm kernels in my ROCm application
expected_behavior: uses rocprof-compute profile -k to filter by kernel name
treats the profile-time -k value as a regex matched against kernel names
